articles.headline: Jalen Duren to begin rehab assignment in next step to return from injury
articles.description: Pistons center Jalen Duren has taken a significant step toward returning from injury, practicing with the team Tuesday.
articles.headlineJa: ジェイレン・デューレン、怪我からの復帰に向けた次なるステップとしてリハビリアサインメントを開始
articles.descriptionJa: ピストンズのセンター、ジェイレン・デューレンが火曜日にチーム練習に合流し、怪我からの復帰に向けて大きな一歩を踏み出した。
articles.body:
ORLANDO, Fla. -- Detroit Pistons center Jalen Duren has taken a significant step toward returning from injury, practicing with the team Tuesday, a day before beginning a rehab assignment.

Duren strained his right hamstring on Oct. 23, in Detroit's second game.

Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff said Duren took part in practice with the team ahead of Tuesday's game against Orlando. But the All-Star will miss his 15th straight game before heading out for a rehab assignment Wednesday with the organization's G League affiliate, the Motor City Cruise.

"We know what he means to our team," Bickerstaff said, "how he can impact us in a positive way. Not only with the physical stuff, but the spirit and mental piece of it."

Duren helped the Pistons to the Eastern Conference playoffs last season, averaging a career-best 19.5 points.

Playing all but two games without Duren this season, Detroit is off to a 10-6 start, tied for fifth in the conference. Third-year forward Ausar Thompson has helped to fill the void left by Duren's absence and has led the team by averaging 8.6 rebounds. Guard Cade Cunningham leads the club in scoring, averaging 24.2 points.

Bickerstaff said he's looking forward to Duren's return.

"He's an anchor for us on both ends of the floor," he said. "With his ability to put the ball in his hands, he can create for himself and create for others."

articles.headline: Bears' Johnson has no plan to forgo Swift's role in run game despite costly fumbles
articles.description: Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift won't have an extended stay in Ben Johnson's doghouse after fumbling in the fourth quarter against the Saints.
articles.headlineJa: ベアーズのジョンソン、痛恨のファンブルにもかかわらず、スウィフトのランゲームにおける役割を外す計画はない
articles.descriptionJa: シカゴ・ベアーズのランニングバック、ドアンドレ・スウィフトは、セインツ戦の第4クォーターでファンブルを犯したが、ベン・ジョンソンの不興を買うことは長くは続かないだろう。
articles.body:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift won't have an extended stay in Ben Johnson's doghouse after fumbling in the fourth quarter against the Saints.

Swift has lost three fumbles through 10 games, which are his most since the 2023 season. The 27-year-old back was pulled from the lineup after New Orleans recovered his fumble at its own 46-yard line and did not return to the game.

That's the second time this season where Swift has been benched in game after fumbling.

Swift's fumbles have gone from an aberration to issue that has become more frequent than at any other point of his Bears tenure. But when asked Tuesday whether Swift needs to regain the trust of his head coach, Johnson rebuffed the idea.

"No, he just needs to hold on to the ball and we'll be fine," Johnson said.

The Bears rushed for 146 yards against the Saints, their third-highest output of the season. Still, Johnson was displeased with the run game's efficiency, spotlighted by Swift's 13 carries for 51 yards (3.9 yards/carry). The veteran back also caught his first touchdown reception of the season.

"We weren't as consistent running the ball as we had wanted to be coming off the bye, that was a point of emphasis for us," Johnson said postgame. "When I looked at our runners, they were under four yards a carry. That efficiency stat that we talked about, we weren't hitting that."

The Bears offense centers heavily around a rushing attack that ranks third league-wide at 142.4 yards per game. That figure would not be possible without Swift, who has played in all 10 games and shouldered a heavier load while running back Kyle Monangai missed five straight weeks with turf toe and a thumb injury. Monangai returned in Week 11 but was limited to eight carries for 18 yards.

With a quick turnaround before facing the Lions on Thanksgiving and seeking their first NFC North win, the Bears are quickly searching for a way to get their run game on track.

From Johnson's perspective, the solution is right in front of them.

"We're going to continue to stress that running game," Johnson said Tuesday. "We got too many good players for it to be lacking behind like it is right now. So, we got to continue to sink into that. It's a big part of what we do and who we are. Whether that's Swift, whether that's Monangai, Salvon [Ahmed] came on and played some big snaps for us. We're going to do that and we're going to continue to possess the ball and those types of things so that opens up our passing game eventually."

Swift ranks 14th in rushing yards (627) and his 10 rushing TDs are tied for the third most in the league. He signed a three-year, $33.75 million contract extension with Chicago prior to Week 1.

articles.headline: Dortmund draw shows that the jury is still out on Gyökeres
articles.description: Brought in to provide the cutting edge that Arsenal needed up front, it's games like Tuesday's draw with Dortmund that show why Viktor Gyökeres continues to divide opinion.
articles.headlineJa: ドルトムントとの引き分け、ギョケレスへの評価は依然として分かれたまま
articles.descriptionJa: アーセナルが前線に必要としていた決定力を補うために獲得されたヴィクトル・ギョケレスだが、火曜日のドルトムント戦のような試合は、なぜ彼の評価が分かれ続けているのかを物語っている。
articles.body:
LONDON -- Anyone who has somehow missed the first 16 months of Viktor Gyökeres' Arsenal career needs to only watch Tuesday's 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund to catch up in full.

For starters, the 28-year-old produced the most devastating moment of his time in north London, smashing in a stunning 28-yard strike to break the deadlock at Emirates Stadium in the 10th minute.

And then, with the game in the balance following Maximilian Beier's 55th-minute equalizer, Gyökeres somehow managed to head wide 6 yards out with the goal gaping. He looked so certain to score that Mikel Arteta began celebrating on the touchline only to stop abruptly when reality struck.

It would be unfair to pin this failure to win solely on Gyökeres. Arsenal ended with 29 shots on goal, hit the woodwork three times and racked up an xG of 2.20 compared with Dortmund's 0.92. The hosts, and reigning Premier League champions, should have won this game.

It follows a familiar pattern of the Gunners failing to press home their advantage seen at Slavia Prague -- when racing into a 2-0 lead and clinging on to a 2-1 win -- and Newcastle United, where they were so absurdly superior for 45 minutes only to score once, then concede twice and scramble a 2-2 draw.

But Gyökeres was the player Arsenal acquired to solve this problem. A €73 million signing from Sporting CP, the Sweden international scored 97 goals in 102 games for the Portuguese side and his arrival was heralded as the No. 9 Arsenal have long needed to take them to the next level.

They won the Premier League for the first time in 22 years, and Gyökeres scored 21 times, but doubts remained over his ability to settle the biggest games. Arteta's team selection toward the end of the previous campaign suggested as much -- using Kai Havertz ahead of Gyökeres -- as did the summer pursuit of an elite attacker which ended in disappointment. And so far this season, Gyökeres has sat behind Havertz in the pecking order, reduced to proving himself in games where Arteta rotated as he did against Dortmund, making six changes with Sunday's Premier League visit of Manchester City in mind.

Since joining the club, Gyökeres has scored more Champions League goals than any other Arsenal player. And this season, he has five goals and four assists in his last 10 games for club and country.

But scratch the surface of that statistic and you realize those interventions have come against Dortmund, Slavia Prague, Fleetwood Town, Poland, Bosnia-Herzegovina (twice) and Romania (twice).

Dortmund are unbeaten in the Bundesliga, sitting two points clear of Bayern Munich and SC Freiburg at the top. They are clearly a talented side -- Beier's equalizer alone was evidence of that -- but ultimately Gyökeres was unable to break a cycle which is in danger of becoming a deeper issue, as much as Arteta continues to suggest otherwise.

articles.headline: Kawhi Leonard's return from knee swelling still at least week away
articles.description: The Raptors say Kawhi Leonard's status will be revisted in a week as he recovers from knee swelling.
articles.headlineJa: カワイ・レナード、膝の腫れによる復帰は少なくともあと1週間先
articles.descriptionJa: ラプターズは、膝の腫れから回復する過程にあるカワイ・レナードの状態について、1週間後に改めて判断すると発表した。
articles.body:
The wait for Kawhi Leonard's return to play from left knee swelling will extend for at least another week.

The Toronto Raptors said Tuesday that the forward "continues to progress in his recovery" and that an update will be provided in a week. Leonard has begun individual on-court workouts after treatment to address the swelling, the Raptors added.

Sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Oct. 27 that Leonard was expected to miss a number of weeks due to swelling in his left knee. An MRI on the knee in September showed no structural damage, and the team has provided weekly updates regarding his status.

Toronto issued a similar message Nov. 17, saying that Leonard "has progressed in his strength and conditioning program." On Nov. 10, the Raptors reported that Leonard would be out at least another week and that he was "continuing his reconditioning process."

Leonard posted a message on X after news initially broke that he would be out, writing that "it's always frustrating missing time."

"I came back to compete with this team and I'm focused on getting back to 100. Toronto, I've appreciated the love since I've been back. Returning soon," he wrote.

The two-time Defensive Player of the Year winner returned to Toronto in the offseason, agreeing to a two-year, $115 million extension after being dealt from the LA Clippers. The trade followed up a tumultuous end to his Clippers tenure. In September, the team was found guilty by the NBA of violating salary cap rules in a case involving Leonard, who wasn't suspended but was fined $700,000.

Coming back to the Raptors, where he led the franchise to its only NBA title in 2019, marked a fresh start for him. So far this season, Leonard has suited up in just two games and is averaging 19.5 points, 7.5 rebounds and 1.5 assists.

The earliest he can return for the 6-11 Raptors is Dec. 1 against the Houston Rockets.

articles.headline: Rasmus Højlund on aiming Man United dig at Man City fans: 'Some good banter'
articles.description: Former United striker Rasmus Hojlund confirmed he shouted "there's only one team in Manchester" towards the City fans after scoring for Napoli.
articles.headlineJa: ラスムス・ホイルンド、マン・シティファンへの挑発について「単なる冗談」と語る
articles.descriptionJa: ナポリで得点を挙げた元ユナイテッドのストライカー、ラスムス・ホイルンドは、シティのファンに向けて「マンチェスターには1チームしかいない」と叫んだことを認めた。
articles.body:
Former Manchester United striker Rasmus Højlund confirmed he shouted "there's only one team in Manchester" towards the Manchester City fans after scoring for Napoli in their Champions League clash at the Etihad on Tuesday. 

Højlund, who scored 14 goals in 62 matches across his three years at Old Trafford, scored the opener in the 2-2 league phase draw.

Asked whether he could confirm he had said the comment, Højlund told TNT Sports: "Yeah, indeed. Yeah, just some good banter. There's the rivalry between Manchester City and Man United, and obviously I have a past in Manchester United, so that's my club. Nothing against Man City, but yeah, United is my club."

Højlund joined Napoli on a season-long loan deal ahead of last season. The switch was made permanent when the club qualified for the Champions League with their second-place finish in Serie A.

He continued: "It's good to score here, good point. And yeah, happy for that."

Ayyoub Bouaddi got City level with his first goal for the club in the second half before Noa Lang put the Italian side back in front. Rayan Cherki rescued a point for the hosts with a solo effort four minutes from time.

The result leaves Enzo Maresca's out-of-form side with just one win from their last seven matches in all competitions. 

- Cherki unhappy despite salvaging Man City draw: 'Don't care about my goal'

Tuesday's encounter marked the return of City legend Kevin De Bruyne to the Etihad after he left for Napoli last year.

De Bruyne, along with Scott McTominay -- another former Man United midfielder -- and Billy Gilmour, was instrumental in helping earn Napoli a point that boosts their hopes of qualifying for the knockout rounds.

"I think the other two gets a lot of praise. Scott and Kevin, incredible players, one of them with an amazing history and Scott doing absolutely fantastic now," Højlund said. "But yeah, sometimes we forget Gilmore and he's done really well this season. He's got more minutes than he did last year."

City, who sit sixth in the league phase table, travel to face Barcelona in their next Champions League outing on Dec. 8 while Napoli host Club Brugge.

articles.headline: Broncos' Sean Payton: J.K. Dobbins suspended one game for detrimental conduct
articles.description: The Broncos suspended running back J.K. Dobbins for one game for conduct detrimental to the team.
articles.headlineJa: ブロンコスのショーン・ペイトン：J.K.ドビンズ、不適切な行為により1試合出場停止
articles.descriptionJa: ブロンコスは、チームに不利益をもたらす行為を行ったとして、ランニングバックのJ.K.ドビンズを1試合出場停止処分とした。
articles.body:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- Denver Broncos coach Sean Payton said Tuesday he has suspended running back J.K. Dobbins for Friday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers due to "conduct detrimental.''

Dobbins will not practice or take part in any team activities this week. The Broncos (8-2) face the Steelers on Friday at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh.

"There is one team announcement, I'm not going to comment afterwards, I'm suspending J.K. Dobbins for this weekend's game, conduct detrimental, that's all I'm going to say about it,'' Payton said after Tuesday's practice. "Head coach's decision.''

Asked if he wanted to elaborate on any of the circumstances that surrounded the decision, Payton said no and added "think it's better that way.''

Dobbins was in the Broncos' facility earlier on Tuesday and then left, multiple team sources said. Payton then told players of the suspension in the team's normally-scheduled group meeting.

Dobbins, in his second season with the team and a player Payton had called one of the "top priorities'' to re-sign this past offseason, had one carry, for no gain, in the Broncos' 38-24 victory Sunday over the Las Vegas Raiders. It marked the first time since the 2020 season Dobbins had a single carry in a game he was in uniform to play -- he had two one-carry games for the Baltimore Ravens that year.

Dobbins was visibly frustrated at times on the sideline during Sunday's game and high-fiving teammates at other times. When asked about the running back rotation Monday, Payton had offered that Dobbins "is healthy'' and that "J.K. is going to be super important for what we're doing in this stretch.''

Jonah Coleman, who sat out four games earlier this season because of an ankle injury, has steadily received more work since his Week 7 return to the lineup. Coleman got 24 of the team's 27 carries by running backs in Sunday's win. Coleman's 111 yards rushing were also the team's first 100-yard rushing game since Dobbins' 111 yards rushing in a Week 8 win last season over the Dallas Cowboys.

The Broncos also designated running back Tyler Badie for return from injured reserve Tuesday and Badie practiced with the team and was listed as a full participant. Asked if Badie would play Friday or how the rotation might look against the Steelers, Payton said, "I'm not going to get into who's playing.''

Running back RJ Harvey (knee) is eligible to return from injured reserve next week.

Quarterback Bo Nix, when asked about the suspension, said: "Well, obviously I have nothing to do with it,'' Nix said. "Just keep finding our way to figure out how to win games, fortunately it has nothing to do with me.''

Cornerback Pat Surtain II, also a team captain like Nix, offered a similar answer with, "I ain't got nothing much to say, it's coach's decision at the end of the day.''

It's all a long way from Dobbins' promise -- he termed it a "pinkie swear'' -- both during the team's minicamp in June as well as training camp, that he would play in every game

articles.headline: Bellingham credits Mourinho 'full stop' for stellar form after Madrid stunner
articles.description: Jude Bellingham praised José Mourinho for helping him reach career-best form after the midfielder scored a stunning goal in Real Madrid's 5-1 comeback win over PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday.
articles.headlineJa: ベリンガム、マドリードでの鮮烈なゴール後、好調の理由は「間違いなく」ムリーニョのおかげと語る
articles.descriptionJa: 火曜日のPSVアイントホーフェン戦における5-1の大逆転勝利で鮮烈なゴールを決めたミッドフィルダーのジュード・ベリンガムは、キャリア最高のコンディションに導いてくれたジョゼ・ムリーニョを称賛した。
articles.body:
Jude Bellingham praised José Mourinho for helping him reach career-best form after the midfielder scored a stunning goal in Real Madrid's 5-1 comeback win over PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday.

Madrid trailed 1-0 at halftime before Mourinho made a triple substitution -- including the introduction of Bellingham -- and the home side then dominated, with Kylian Mbappé netting a brace, and Vinícius Júnior scoring his first Champions League goal this season.

Madrid are now top of the league phase table with 15 points after winning all five UCL matches so far, with a visit to Arsenal in their next European game on Dec. 9.

"Mourinho. Full stop," Bellingham told journalists at the Bernabéu, when asked to explain his outstanding form, with four goals in his last five club games. "I'm enjoying my football a lot. I love the coach, his staff, and my teammates help me a lot.

"That's why I'm playing well, because I have a lot of help."

Bellingham was asked if his displays with England at the World Cup -- where he scored seven goals playing behind Harry Kane -- had been the catalyst for his renewed goal threat.

"I don't know if it's because I'm playing as a number 10, it's having freedom," Bellingham said. " Freedom to move, to drop deep, to help build up, and to play higher up to finish.

"I think Mourinho has given me a lot of confidence. That's why I'm playing well, because I'm happy."

Madrid have now beaten Inter Milan, Roma, RB Leipzig, AEK Athens and PSV in the Champions League this season, despite some inconsistent performances.

"The second half was a question of mentality," Mourinho told Movistar. "We made changes, and Jude is a different player. He gives us what we didn't have in the first [half].

"It was a mental 'click.' In the first half we didn't find our rhythm, we didn't press, we didn't win duels."

Mourinho refused to reveal if he'd been angry with his players in the dressing room at halftime.

"The dressing room is like Vegas," the coach said. "What happens in Vegas, stays in Vegas.

"We spoke. We're friends, and we spoke."

"Once again, the first half wasn't good," goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois said. "In modern football, if we don't all run and do what the manager asks of us, it's impossible, especially against a team that presses you man-to-man.

"With the clips [Mourinho] showed us on the screen at halftime, you could see we weren't doing things right. That changed our attitude."

Madrid, who are three points behind LaLiga leaders Barcelona, next play Alaves at the Bernabeu on Nov. 28.

articles.headline: Arteta questions 'how in hell' Arsenal didn't score more in Dortmund draw
articles.description: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta rued his side's failure to put Borussia Dortmund away as "unbelievable."
articles.headlineJa: アルテタ、ドルトムント戦の引き分けを受け「一体全体どうやって」もっと得点できなかったのかと疑問を呈す
articles.descriptionJa: アーセナルのミケル・アルテタ監督は、ボルシア・ドルトムントを仕留めきれなかったチームの不甲斐なさを「信じられない」と悔やんだ。
articles.body:
Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta rued his side's failure to put Borussia Dortmund away as "unbelievable" after watching the Premier League champions create 30 shots before drawing 1-1 at the Emirates Stadium.

Viktor Gyökeres crashed in Arsenal's opener after 10 minutes of Tuesday's Champions League contest, but for the second time in as many games, following their 2-2 draw at Newcastle, Arteta's men were unable to see out the victory after Maximilian Beier's second-half equalizer.

Olley: Dortmund draw shows that the jury is still out on Gyökeres

Arsenal hit a post three times in response, while Gyökeres also wasted a golden opportunity to restore his side's advantage when he headed wide from six yards with 15 minutes left. In all, Arsenal found the target just four times.

Although Arteta was pleased with his side's dominant display, against a team that  occupies top spot in the Bundesliga, he was left to reflect on what might have been.

"It was a brilliant performance," he said. "The way we played, bearing in mind the opposition, is something I can be very, very pleased about because there is very little more that you can demand from the team.

"But obviously, the feeling is we should reward ourselves much more when you put in that kind of performance and get those amount of chances.

"There is an element of luck, and an element of us finishing the actions better. There's no question how superior, how dominant, and how much of a threat we were. It was great to watch, but it was unbelievable that sometimes the ball didn't end up in the back of the net.

"I don't know if it is our mentality. As I said, there was an element of luck, because how in hell have some of the goals not gone in?"

The draw extended last season's finalists' unbeaten streak in the Champions League to 20 games but ended their 12-game home winning streak in league phase.

Arsenal now sit in fifth position ahead of the completion of the fifth round of matches on Wednesday. The top eight qualify automatically for the round of 16.

Tuesday saw goalkeeper Kepa Arrizabalaga handed a rare appearance in place of David Raya.

Arteta is uncertain if his number one -- injured against Newcastle on Saturday -- will be fit to face Manchester City in the Premier League this weekend.

"I have nothing to add to that unfortunately," he said. "We need to know first how bad it is and whether he has a chance or not to make it."

Arsenal might have had the lion's share of shots, but Jobe Bellingham had a goal ruled out for offside for Dortmund. Gyökeres could also count himself fortunate not to give away a penalty when a Dortmund corner struck him on the arm in the second half.

"I thought VAR should have looked at the handball. It would have been worth a check," Dortmund coach Niko Kovac said.

"They are trying to intervene less with the on-field decisions, but it doesn't mean you should not intervene when you should do.

articles.headline: Tyrese, Jade Haliburton announce they are expecting their first child
articles.description: The couple wed in August after seven years of dating and announced the news that they're expecting on Instagram.
articles.headlineJa: タイリースとジェイド・ハリバートン、第一子の妊娠を発表
articles.descriptionJa: 7年間の交際を経て8月に結婚した二人は、Instagramを通じて第一子を授かったことを発表した。
articles.body:
Indiana Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton and his wife, Jade, are expecting their first child, the couple announced Tuesday in a joint post on Instagram.

They shared the news with a photoshoot that featured their apricot labradoodle, Ames, wearing an apron that said "Big Brother" and their ultrasound image.

The comments were flooded with congratulations from athletes and teams such as gymnast Simone Biles, Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark, New York Liberty forward Breanna Stewart, Los Angeles Sparks center Cameron Brink, San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle, the Fever and the Pacers.

Haliburton's current and former teammates Andrew Nembhard, James Johnson and Jay Huff also chimed in, as did the Golden State Warriors' Georges Niang and Charlotte Hornets' Grant Williams.

The post's caption reads: "Baby Hali. Spring 2027."

The Haliburtons wed in August after getting engaged in July 2025 and being together for seven years. The couple met while attending Iowa State. Jade was a cheerleader, and Tyrese played two seasons with the Cyclones before being drafted in 2020.

The Pacers guard tore his right Achilles tendon in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals, sidelining him for all of the 2025-26 season. He returned this season and averaged 21.8 points, 9.5 assists and 4.5 rebounds in four games until suffering a hamstring strain that has kept him out since Oct. 26.

articles.headline: Brandon Aiyuk scheduled for visit Wednesday with Commanders, agent says
articles.description: Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is scheduled to visit Wednesday with the Commanders, agent Drew Rosenhaus told ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.headlineJa: ブランドン・アイユク、水曜日にコマンダーズを訪問予定、代理人が明かす
articles.descriptionJa: ワイドレシーバーのブランドン・アイユクは、水曜日にコマンダーズを訪問する予定であると、代理人のドリュー・ローゼンハウスがESPNのアダム・シェフターに語った。
articles.body:
Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is scheduled to visit Wednesday with the Washington Commanders, agent Drew Rosenhaus told ESPN's Adam Schefter.

The San Francisco 49ers released Aiyuk on Tuesday, two weeks after the NFL reinstated him. He cleared waivers, making him an unrestricted free agent.

Aiyuk has not played since tearing the ACL, MCL and meniscus in his right knee on Oct. 20, 2024, and was placed on the 49ers' reserve/left squad list last December. He could not be removed from that list until he reported and passed a physical, which he did Nov. 9.

"I'm feeling great, feeling healthy," Aiyuk told 49ers reporters earlier this month. "It was a long recovery process, a long rehab process, but I'm back to 100%."

Aiyuk is expected to work out for the Commanders during Wednesday's visit.

In 2023, his last full season before his injury, Aiyuk was named second-team All-Pro after catching 75 passes for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns.

Aiyuk and Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels played together at Arizona State during the 2019 season. However, a rift in their relationship appeared to have developed following a series of social media posts by the receiver. Aiyuk targeted Daniels in several posts and in one referenced Daniels' mother.

Daniels and Aiyuk spoke more than a month ago to clear the air, according to multiple sources.

Daniels befriended Aiyuk early in their time together at ASU -- before Daniels had won the starting quarterback job. During workouts, Daniels would throw with Aiyuk, who was going into his senior season and coming off a 33-catch, 474-yard season.

They quickly developed a rapport as Aiyuk ended the season with Associated Press All-America honors after catching 65 passes for 1,192 yards and eight touchdowns.

ESPN's John Keim contributed to this report.
